商品评论_完整文本:
Flavor and texture of this type of rice make it perfect for risotto. For one thing, the grains maintain their shape better than arborio rice. This feature truly sets it apart and makes it perfect for certain types of risotto in the same way that some pasta shapes are better than others depending on the sauce.

I use carnaroli rice when I am basing the risotto on larger pieces of fish such as monkfish and mahi. The firmer grains work better with ingredients like that. I also use it when I want to make a very creamy risotto, which is another feature of this type of rice. It has an even higher starch content than arborio rice.

The only real drawback as far as I can tell is carnaroli does not absorb saffron nearly as well as arborio, so when I am preparing a risotto that has saffron I use arborio rice instead. As an aside, I recommend [[ASIN:B0042ZF6B2 Iranian Saffron]] for any dishes that call for saffron. That particular brand is of exceptional quality.

Regarding the portion size I think that the 16-ounce portions of this particular brand is about 4-ounces more than you need to make a risotto for up to eight people. I save the excess from each box in a sealed plastic container, so for me this six-box set is more like eight boxes. Since I do not cook risotto more than twice a month (and often less) this package is a six month supply for me, which makes the price a bargain.

One final note: I tend to use about ten percent more stock for this rice than I do for arborio grains, and I also tack on an additional five minutes of cooking time when using carnaroli. Your times will probably vary, but take into consideration that you may need a little more stock and cooking time if you are switching from arborio to carnaroli for risotto recipes.

Buon appetito!
